To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully fabricated a free-standing Ti microbridge on a Si membrane with the thickness of 40 and 64 nm and measured its electrical and thermal properties, which are important for the design of a large array of TES.
we have developed a free-standing superconducting Ti membrane with a twin-slot antenna and a Ti microbridge.
the Ti TES on free-standing membrane is a promising candidate for the large TES array readout.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and fabrication of a free-standing membrane supported superconducting Ti TES with reduced thermal conductance, improved uniformity and reduced effective response time.
the characterization of a free-standing Ti TES supported by a membrane and its uniformity study.
the characterization of the free-standing Ti microbridge supported by a thin membrane and the improvement of the uniformity of the array.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the free-standing membrane supported superconducting Ti TES has been successfully fabricated.

the free-standing membrane supported microbridge TES has a lower transition temperature, a lower normal resistance, a lower thermal conductance and a shorter effective response time than the substrate-supported microbridge TES.
a free-standing membrane supported superconducting Ti TES has the potential for a high performance TES array.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the free-standing membrane supported TES is a promising candidate for the future X-ray microcalorimeter.
the free-standing membrane supported superconducting Ti transition edge sensor is a promising candidate for large array detector.
the free-standing membrane supported superconducting Ti TES is a promising candidate for the read out of a large TES array with high speed and low noise.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the free-standing membrane supported superconducting Ti TES can achieve the same or even better performance as the substrate supported Ti TES.
the free-standing membrane supported superconducting Ti transition edge sensor has the potential to be a candidate of large TES arrays.
a free-standing superconducting Ti TES with reduced transition temperature and increased normal resistance can be realized by wet etching the substrate.
